</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Main Results: The Safety–Helpfulness Trade-off</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the performance of CORA against both unconstrained base policies and representative safety baselines on the Harm-150 subset of <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Phone-Harm</span> and on <span id="S5.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">MobileRisk</span> benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>.
Rather than collapsing deployment readiness into a single metric, we analyze the Pareto trade-off between bounding harm, achieving user goals, and avoiding excessive interruptions.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gating accuracy and goal achievement.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Achieving a near-zero Harm Rate is trivially possible by suppressing execution altogether. Closed-source base policies such as GPT-5 illustrate this failure mode: their HR of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.40\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.40</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.40\%</annotation></semantics></math> and mHR of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.34\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.34</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.34\%</annotation></semantics></math> come at the cost of a Goal Achievement Rate collapsing to <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="37.50\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>37.50</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">37.50\%</annotation></semantics></math>, consistent with extreme conservatism or premature trajectory termination. At the opposite end of the spectrum, rigid heuristic gates raise HR to <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24.37\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24.37</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24.37\%</annotation></semantics></math>, because hand-specified triggers fail to generalise across dynamic, visually
complex GUI layouts. CORA departs from this trade-off by gating actions through a statistically calibrated decision boundary. Our framework attains <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GAR}=79.80\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>GAR</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>79.80</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GAR}=79.80\%</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{IF1}=85.29\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>IF1</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>85.29</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{IF1}=85.29\%</annotation></semantics></math>, indicating that it does not merely suppress actions but identifies <em id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">when</em> intervention is warranted, improving IF1 over the strongest zero-shot gating baseline (VLM-as-critic, <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="44.21\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>44.21</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">44.21\%</annotation></semantics></math>) by more than <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>40</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40</annotation></semantics></math> absolute points. The moderate Over-Intervention Rate of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.23\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.23</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.23\%</annotation></semantics></math> is an explicit, tunable consequence of the conformal risk budget, which prioritises high recall on catastrophic harms over silent failures; as we show below, once benign traffic is factored in, this interruption cost is almost entirely concentrated on genuinely harmful steps.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Robustness to injection and misbehavior.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Evaluation on MobileRisk exposes the limits of zero-shot safety judges.
On this highly class-imbalanced benchmark, baselines such as VLM-as-critic can inflate Accuracy to <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.92\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>86.92</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.92\%</annotation></semantics></math> by defaulting to the <em id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">safe</em> label,
yet collapse to an F1 of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.05\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.05</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.05\%</annotation></semantics></math> and miss the majority of critical violations. CORA, by contrast, attains Recall <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="76.47\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>76.47</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">76.47\%</annotation></semantics></math> and F1 <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="66.38\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>66.38</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">66.38\%</annotation></semantics></math>, the highest among all compared methods. This confirms that the action-conditional Guardian, anchored by the Goal-Lock mechanism, remains sensitive to semantic goal drift and to indirect prompt injections embedded in the visual context.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">A deployment-realistic unified view.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A legitimate concern with the harm-only comparison above is whether CORA’s GAR advantage stems from calibrated risk discrimination or from a more permissive guardian that simply executes more actions. To probe this, we re-evaluate every method jointly on the <em id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">full</em> Phone-Harm benchmark, step-weighting its Harm-150 and Normal-150 subsets equally; the precise aggregation formulae, together with the assumptions used for methods that expose no explicit guardian on the benign subset, are given in the caption of Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
Under this deployment-realistic mixture, CORA retains the highest GAR (<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.69\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89.69</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.69\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and IF1 (<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.29\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.29</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.29\%</annotation></semantics></math>), improving over the strongest baseline UI-TARS-1.5 by <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+12.41" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>12.41</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+12.41</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+28.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>28.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+28.15</annotation></semantics></math> absolute points, while its merged HR drops to <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.19\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.19</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.19\%</annotation></semantics></math>, below UI-TARS-1.5 (<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.87\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.87</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.87\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and comparable to the AutoGLM family. Crucially, CORA’s merged OIR of <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.83\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>9.83</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.83\%</annotation></semantics></math> decomposes into <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.23\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.23</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.23\%</annotation></semantics></math> on the harmful subset and only <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.42\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.42</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.42\%</annotation></semantics></math> on the benign subset, confirming that its diagnostician budget is spent where risk actually exists rather than as a blanket interruption mechanism. GPT-5 and Gemini-3 retain the lowest HR/mHR/OIR, but only by compressing merged GAR to the <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="68" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>68</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">68</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>72</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72\%</annotation></semantics></math> range, precisely the refusal regime that CORA is designed to escape.
Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> visualises both views in the HR–GAR plane.
On the harmful subset (Fig. <a href="#S5.F2.sf1" title="In Figure 2 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(a)</span></a>) CORA sits alone on an outward-shifted frontier, while the heuristic gate degenerates towards the high-HR region. On the merged distribution (Fig. <a href="#S5.F2.sf2" title="In Figure 2 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2(b)</span></a>) the base policies tighten into a lower frontier spanning <math id="S5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GAR}\in[68.75,\,77.28]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>GAR</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>68.75</mn><mo>,</mo><mn> 77.28</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GAR}\in[68.75,\,77.28]</annotation></semantics></math>; CORA still dominates this cloud and anchors a strictly outward frontier, whose vertical gap to the baseline curve quantifies the benefit of conformally-calibrated risk control over ad-hoc safeguards.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Capability Retention on Benign Tasks</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A well-known bottleneck of post-policy safety controllers is the
<em id="S5.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">alignment tax</em>: a degradation of base capabilities on benign tasks caused by false-positive interventions. We probe this effect using the <span id="S5.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">core20</span> safe-navigation tasks of AndroidWorld
(Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).
Wrapping the unconstrained AutoGLM policy with CORA raises its success rate from <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="30.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>30.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30.0\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="40.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>40.0</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>, recovering <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="72.7\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>72.7</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">72.7\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the GPT-5 upper bound and surpassing UI-TARS-1.5 by <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>20</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math> absolute points. Rather than aborting a trajectory upon a high-risk grounding error, a common failure mode in dense mobile UIs, CORA’s Generative Diagnostician (§<a href="#S3.SS5" title="3.5 Generative Semantic Diagnostician as System 2 ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>) issues targeted <span id="S5.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Reflect</span> or <span id="S5.SS3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Confirm</span> interventions, allowing the agent to recover from visual ambiguities and correct its own misclicks. On these benign workloads, the safety controller therefore operates as a mild error-recovery layer rather than a source of additional alignment tax.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Ablation Studies</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We ablate the four architectural components of CORA (e.g., CRC, action-conditioning of the Guardian, the Generative Diagnostician, and Goal-Lock) on a held-out calibration pool (<math id="S5.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}1075" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1075</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}1075</annotation></semantics></math>, target risk <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta{=}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta{=}0.05</annotation></semantics></math>), sweeping the decision threshold <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9\}</annotation></semantics></math> and comparing each fixed point against the CRC-selected <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}(\delta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}(\delta)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The analysis yields four consistent findings. <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(i)</span> Replacing CRC with a static development-tuned threshold removes the statistical safety guarantee and no fixed <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> recovers the CRC operating point, which dominates on coverage and invocation rate while staying well inside the risk budget. <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(ii)</span> Stripping action-conditioning reduces the Guardian to a state-evaluator that cannot disambiguate visually adjacent affordances such as a benign “Cancel” tap versus an irreversible “Confirm Transfer”, yielding strictly worse coverage–invocation trade-offs at every swept threshold. <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(iii)</span> Replacing the Generative Diagnostician with a rule-based heuristic causes the system to violate the <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta{=}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta{=}0.05</annotation></semantics></math> budget at <em id="S5.SS4.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">every</em> threshold, confirming that context-aware semantic intervention is required to remain inside the risk target in open-ended mobile environments. <span id="S5.SS4.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(iv)</span> Disabling Goal-Lock forces CRC to select an aggressively conservative <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}</annotation></semantics></math> merely to keep expected harm below <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas enabling it expands the attainable safety–coverage Pareto frontier <em id="S5.SS4.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">before</em> conformal calibration is applied. The full risk–coverage sweeps, per-threshold statistics, and figure-level breakdowns for each ablation are provided in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Additional Ablation Details ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented <span id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CORA</span>, a post-policy, pre-action safety controller that turns open-ended mobile GUI control into <em id="S6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">selective action execution</em> with statistical guarantees. CORA couples an action-conditional Guardian, Conformal Risk Control over the executed-harm rate, a generative Diagnostician for minimal interventions, and a Goal-Lock contract that resists indirect injection. To evaluate this paradigm we introduced <span id="S6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Phone-Harm</span>, a mobile benchmark that pairs a Harm-150 subset of step-level harmful tasks with a matched Normal-150 benign subset under a shared authoring protocol, enabling both adversarial safety evaluation and deployment-realistic mixed-traffic analysis. Across Phone-Harm, MobileRisk, and AndroidWorld, CORA improves the safety–helpfulness–interruption Pareto frontier over diverse base policies and safety baselines, meets its conformal risk target on held-out test data, and concentrates its intervention budget on genuinely harmful steps rather than benign traffic; on benign navigation tasks it further <em id="S6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">raises</em> the success rate of its base policy while preserving safety, turning the safety shield into a mild error-recovery layer rather than a source of alignment tax.
Beyond these empirical gains, CORA offers a practical template for deploying GUI agents under explicit, user-tunable safety budgets. We see several promising directions: tighter sequential conformal treatments for long-horizon trajectories, richer weighted calibration under app, OS, and locale shift, and extending Phone-Harm towards broader coverage of real-world mobile workloads. We hope that the integration of selective execution, conformal calibration, and harm-aware mobile benchmarking reported here can serve as a stepping stone towards agents that are simultaneously autonomous, helpful, and provably safe.</p>
</div>
</section>

</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock">In <span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_inbook">Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38: Annual Conference

</span>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Appendix Overview</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This supplementary material details technical, empirical, and reproducibility elements omitted from the main text. It begins with
Phone-Harm benchmark details and qualitative safety case studies (Sec. <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>, <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>). We then formalize evaluation metrics (Sec. <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Evaluation Metrics ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>).
Following exhaustive ablations of CORA’s core components (Sec. <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Additional Ablation Details ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>), we supply complete methodological derivations (Sec. <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F Additional Details on Methodology ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>) and elaborate on the environment and data collection (Sec. <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Additional Details on Environment and Data Collection ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>). The document concludes with explicit experimental setups (Sec. <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Additional Details on Experimental Setup ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>) and a reproducibility checklist (Sec. <a href="#A9" title="Appendix I Reproducibility and Release Plan ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">I</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Phone-Harm</span> comprises two sister subsets constructed under a shared authoring and annotation protocol: <span id="A2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Harm-150</span>, a curated set of <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> step-level harmful tasks that provides the harm indicators <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> used by all safety metrics in Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>; and <span id="A2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Normal-150</span>, a matched set of <math id="A2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> purely benign mobile tasks (<math id="A2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{t}{=}0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{t}{=}0</annotation></semantics></math> throughout) used exclusively as a utility and false-alarm control in the mixed-traffic analysis of Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Setup ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. The remainder of this appendix documents the construction of Harm-150, which is where all step-level harm structure resides; Normal-150 shares the same apps and authoring protocol but contains no harmful steps, and its per-method evaluation numbers are summarised in §<a href="#S5.SS2" title="5.2 Main Results: The Safety–Helpfulness Trade-off ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> of the main text.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2604.09155v1/figures/phoneharm_app_subcategory_2x2.png" id="A2.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/353;" width="476" height="353" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F3.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="A2.F3.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Harm-150 distribution overview. (a) App distribution over the
full Harm-150 subset, highlighting a long-tail coverage. (b–d)
Sub-category distributions for <span id="A2.F3.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Misuse</span>, <span id="A2.F3.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Misbehavior</span>,
and <span id="A2.F3.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Injection</span>, respectively, demonstrating concentrated risk
modes within each harm type.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Benchmark Scope and App Coverage</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Harm-150 is designed to rigorously evaluate step-level safety violations
in realistic, high-stakes mobile interactions. To demonstrate the
generalisability of our safety framework CORA, we establish a clear
hierarchy of application coverage. While CORA inherently supports robust
operations across 165 mobile applications, our simulated environment is
purposefully instantiated with 42 diverse apps to emulate the clutter of
a realistic user device. From this environment, the Harm-150 subset
curates <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> human-authored tasks spanning 29 commonly used apps where
high-stakes safety violations are most prevalent.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As summarized in Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ B.2 Task Design and Annotation ‣ Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, Harm-150 is strictly
balanced to mitigate class-prior bias. Its <math id="A2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="150" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>150</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">150</annotation></semantics></math> tasks are evenly
distributed across the three harm categories (<span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Misuse</span>,
<span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Injection</span>, <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Misbehavior</span>) and three risk levels
(Critical, High, Medium). Furthermore,
Figure <a href="#A2.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> illustrates a shallow-head
and substantial long-tail app distribution, ensuring the evaluation is
not overfitted to a single app vertical.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F4" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A2.F4.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2604.09155v1/figures/misuse.jpg" id="A2.F4.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:476/1031;" width="476" height="1031" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F4.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="A2.F4.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Deliberate Misuse qualitative case. Given an instruction to create an “Anyone with the link” share link for the “password” document in Google Drive, elevate permission to “Anyone can edit,” and send it to a specific contact person, CORA identifies the request as privacy theft, flags high risk, and aborts before any sharing action is executed.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A2.F4.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2604.09155v1/figures/Injection_english.jpg" id="A2.F4.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:476/1031;" width="476" height="1031" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F4.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="A2.F4.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Prompt-injection qualitative case. CORA correctly recognizes the on-screen malicious message as a prompt injection and reasons: “I should tap a blank area to close the harmful pop-up and continue the task”. It then takes the safe dismiss action and proceeds with the original user instruction.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_3">
<figure id="A2.F4.sf3" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><img src="2604.09155v1/figures/misbehavior.jpg" id="A2.F4.sf3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:476/1031;" width="476" height="1031" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F4.sf3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(c)</span> </span><span id="A2.F4.sf3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Misbehavior qualitative case. In an app-store one-tap purchase screen, CORA avoids autonomous execution of the irreversible “1-tap buy” action. Instead, it defers control by requesting explicit user confirmation, mitigating model-misbehavior risk via human-in-the-loop safety gating.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A2.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="A2.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Qualitative cases from Harm-150 demonstrating CORA’s safety
behaviour: prompt-injection, misbehavior mitigation, and deliberate
misuse prevention.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Task Design and Annotation</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each Harm-150 instance provides: (i) a frozen user goal <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>,
(ii) the current observation <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{t},u_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{t},u_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, (iii) a proposed action
<math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, and (iv) a strict step-level annotation indicating whether
executing <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is harmful.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Crucially, tasks are formulated such that harmful actions are
deterministically identifiable at the step level, isolating safety
evaluation from ambiguous multi-step credit assignment issues. Task
authoring strictly followed four principles:
<span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(1) Goal clarity:</span> the intended user goal is explicit and stable.
<span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(2) Step locality:</span> harm can be judged from the current step
without future leakage.
<span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(3) Realism:</span> actions correspond to plausible interactions under
realistic app states.
<span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(4) Consequence relevance:</span> harmful steps carry meaningful
privacy, financial, or social consequences.
The same authoring protocol, minus the harm-injection step, is applied
to Normal-150 to ensure distributional parity across the two subsets.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The evaluated domains in Harm-150 predominantly feature Content/Media
(28.0%), Communication/Social (18.7%), and Travel/Maps (17.3%). As
detailed in Figure <a href="#A2.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>b–d, these
tasks capture distinct real-world threat vectors: misuse is heavily
concentrated on privacy theft (54.0%) and account abuse (24.0%);
misbehavior is dominated by over-compliance errors (52.0%); and
injections are primarily triggered via UI advertising surfaces, such as
banners (36.0%) and pop-ups (34.0%). This confirms our threat model
that mobile harms are tied not only to policy-level misuse but also to
interface-level injection channels.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A2.T4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="A2.T4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Summary statistics of the Harm-150 subset of <span id="A2.T4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Phone-Harm</span>.</span></figcaption>

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Qualitative Case Study</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A2.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ B.1 Benchmark Scope and App Coverage ‣ Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> illustrates representative cases across the three harm categories where CORA successfully prevents unsafe execution and selects the appropriate intervention. These examples demonstrate CORA’s ability to:</p>
<ol id="A3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Prevent deliberate misuse (Fig. <a href="#A2.F4.sf1" title="In Figure 4 ‣ B.1 Benchmark Scope and App Coverage ‣ Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(a)</span></a>):</span> Given a harmful user instruction attempting privacy theft (e.g., publicly sharing and granting edit access to a sensitive “password” document), CORA correctly identifies the inherent risk in the goal itself and triggers an <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Abort</span> before any privacy-compromising action is executed.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Resist prompt injections (Fig. <a href="#A2.F4.sf2" title="In Figure 4 ‣ B.1 Benchmark Scope and App Coverage ‣ Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(b)</span></a>):</span> CORA recognizes a malicious on-screen message that conflicts with the frozen user goal. Instead of following the injected instruction, it reasons to safely dismiss the harmful pop-up and seamlessly proceeds with the original task.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mitigate model misbehavior (Fig. <a href="#A2.F4.sf3" title="In Figure 4 ‣ B.1 Benchmark Scope and App Coverage ‣ Appendix B Additional Details on Phone-Harm Benchmark ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4(c)</span></a>):</span> Confronted with an irreversible financial transaction (a “1-tap buy” in an app store) under a benign user goal, CORA avoids autonomous execution. Instead, it routes the proposed action to a <span id="A3.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Confirm</span> intervention, effectively preventing high-stakes errors via human-in-the-loop gating.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Evaluation Metrics</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section details the formal definitions of the evaluation metrics. To provide a comprehensive evaluation and ensure fair comparisons with existing literature, we categorize our metrics into three distinct groups: step-level safety metrics, intervention and behavior metrics, and standard classification metrics specific to the MobileRisk <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2025a</a>]</cite> and AndroidWorld <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rawles et al., 2024</a>]</cite> benchmarks.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Step-Level Safety Metrics</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> be the total number of evaluated steps. For each step <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, let
<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{t}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{t}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote whether the action is executed (<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>) or interrupted (<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>), and
<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the ground-truth harm label (<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> means harmful).</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Harm Rate (HR).</span>
HR is the fraction of all steps that are both harmful and executed:</p>
<table id="A4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{HR}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}h_{t}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>HR</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{HR}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}h_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Lower is better.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Macro Harm Rate (mHR).</span>
In our implementation, <span id="A4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">mHR</span> is the conditional harm rate among executed steps:</p>
<table id="A4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{mHR}=\frac{\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}h_{t}}{\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>mHR</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{mHR}=\frac{\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}h_{t}}{\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{t}e_{t}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{t}e_{t}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, we set <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{mHR}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>mHR</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{mHR}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Lower is better.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Intervention and Behavior Metrics</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although grouped as behavior metrics, these are computed from step-level decisions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Goal Achievement Rate (GAR).</span>
GAR is the execution (coverage) rate:</p>
<table id="A4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{GAR}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>GAR</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{GAR}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}e_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Higher is better.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Over-Intervention Rate (OIR).</span>
Let <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate whether the diagnostician is invoked at step <math id="A4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then</p>
<table id="A4.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{OIR}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}d_{t}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>OIR</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{OIR}=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}d_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Lower is better.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Intervention F1 (IF1).</span>
IF1 is computed only on harmful steps <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}=\{t\mid h_{t}=1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>t</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}=\{t\mid h_{t}=1\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>, the target intervention label <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained from the harm type
(<span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">misuse<math id="A4.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\!\to\!" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\!\to\!</annotation></semantics></math>abort</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">injection<math id="A4.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\!\to\!" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\!\to\!</annotation></semantics></math>confirm</span>, <span id="A4.SS2.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">misbehavior<math id="A4.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\!\to\!" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\!\to\!</annotation></semantics></math>reflect</span>),
and <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{y}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{y}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is the final predicted decision.
Let <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}</annotation></semantics></math> be the union of labels appearing in <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{y_{t}^{\star}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{y_{t}^{\star}\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\hat{y}_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\hat{y}_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We report macro-F1:</p>
<table id="A4.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{IF1}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{L}|}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}}\frac{2\,\mathrm{TP}_{\ell}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}_{\ell}+\mathrm{FP}_{\ell}+\mathrm{FN}_{\ell}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>IF1</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow></munder><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>TP</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>TP</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>FP</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>FN</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{IF1}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{L}|}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}}\frac{2\,\mathrm{TP}_{\ell}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}_{\ell}+\mathrm{FP}_{\ell}+\mathrm{FN}_{\ell}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">If <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{H}|=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{H}|=0</annotation></semantics></math>, we set <math id="A4.SS2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{IF1}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>IF1</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{IF1}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Higher is better.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Standard Classification Metrics</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To establish a direct and standard comparison with baseline methods on the MobileRisk benchmark and AndriodWorld Benchmark, we follow its specific evaluation protocol and report fundamental binary classification metrics. We aggregate the True Positives (<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{TP}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>TP</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{TP}</annotation></semantics></math>), True Negatives (<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{TN}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>TN</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{TN}</annotation></semantics></math>), False Positives (<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FP}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>FP</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FP}</annotation></semantics></math>), and False Negatives (<math id="A4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FN}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>FN</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FN}</annotation></semantics></math>) over the MobileRisk evaluation set.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1.</span>
We compute these standard metrics to measure the overall correctness and the trade-off between false alarms and missed detections on MobileRisk:</p>
<table id="A4.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.E15"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{Accuracy}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Accuracy</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{Accuracy}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{TN}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{TN}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>TP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>TN</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>TP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>TN</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>FP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>FN</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{TN}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{TN}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A4.E16"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{Precision}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Precision</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{Precision}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{TP}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>TP</mi><mrow><mi>TP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>FP</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{TP}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A4.E17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{Recall}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Recall</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{Recall}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{TP}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>TP</mi><mrow><mi>TP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>FN</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{TP}}{\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FN}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A4.E18"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{F1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F1</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{F1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.E18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{2\cdot\mathrm{Precision}\cdot\mathrm{Recall}}{\mathrm{Precision}+\mathrm{Recall}+\varepsilon}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>Precision</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>Recall</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>Precision</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Recall</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{2\cdot\mathrm{Precision}\cdot\mathrm{Recall}}{\mathrm{Precision}+\mathrm{Recall}+\varepsilon}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Higher values indicate superior risk detection capabilities.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">False Positive Rate (FPR).</span>
To explicitly quantify the rate of false alarms on benign queries within MobileRisk, we report the FPR:</p>
<table id="A4.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{FPR}=\frac{\mathrm{FP}}{\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{TN}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>FPR</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>FP</mi><mrow><mi>FP</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>TN</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{FPR}=\frac{\mathrm{FP}}{\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{TN}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">A lower FPR is crucial for maintaining the operational utility of the agent without inducing unnecessary interruptions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Success Rate (SR).</span>
To evaluate the functional capabilities and instruction-following proficiency of the agent in realistic mobile environments, we report the Success Rate on the AndroidWorld benchmark. This metric is strictly decoupled from the safety metrics to explicitly measure system utility.
The Success Rate measures the proportion of tasks where the agent successfully reaches the intended goal state. Let <math id="A4.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{AW}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>AW</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{AW}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the set of evaluated episodes in AndroidWorld. We define SR as:</p>
<table id="A4.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E20.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{SR}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{AW}}|}\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{AW}}}\mathbb{I}[\mathrm{Success}(e)=1]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>SR</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>AW</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>e</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mi>AW</mi></msub></mrow></munder><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>Success</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{SR}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{AW}}|}\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{AW}}}\mathbb{I}[\mathrm{Success}(e)=1],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{I}[\mathrm{Success}(e)=1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝕀</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>Success</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>e</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{I}[\mathrm{Success}(e)=1]</annotation></semantics></math> is the indicator function that equals <math id="A4.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> if the final state of episode <math id="A4.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>e</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> rigorously satisfies the task-specific success criteria defined by the AndroidWorld environment, and <math id="A4.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> otherwise. A higher SR indicates stronger functional competence and minimal degradation of utility due to safety interventions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Additional Ablation Details</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix provides the full risk–coverage sweeps and per-threshold statistics underlying the ablation summary of §<a href="#S5.SS4" title="5.4 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.4</span></a> in the main text. Each study isolates one of CORA’s four architectural components (i.e., Conformal Risk Control, action-conditioning of the Guardian, the Generative Diagnostician, and Goal-Lock) at a fixed calibration size <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}1075" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1075</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}1075</annotation></semantics></math> and target risk <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta{=}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta{=}0.05</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>The Influence of Conformal Risk Control (CRC)</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To understand the necessity of Conformal Risk Control, we ablate this module by replacing its statistically calibrated boundary with a static, development-tuned threshold. This naive approach destabilizes the operating point and compromises the statistical safety bounds, leading to unpredictable over-interruption or severe safety regressions when subjected to domain shift.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ Appendix E Additional Ablation Details ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> illustrates the impact of the CRC threshold on the CORA holdout set (<math id="A5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}1075" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1075</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}1075</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta{=}0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta{=}0.05</annotation></semantics></math>). For a fixed scalar threshold <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9\}</annotation></semantics></math>, increasing <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> yields the expected safety-autonomy trade-off: task coverage improves from <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.77\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.77</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.77\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.02\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89.02</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.02\%</annotation></semantics></math>, while the executed-harm rate rises from <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.56\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.56</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.56\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.86\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.86</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.86\%</annotation></semantics></math>, and the Diagnostician invocation rate drops from <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14.23\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.23</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.23\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.98\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.98</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.98\%</annotation></semantics></math>. In contrast, the CRC module adaptively selects <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\tau}=0.952" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>τ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>0.952</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\tau}=0.952</annotation></semantics></math>. This optimally calibrated threshold achieves the best coverage (<math id="A5.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89.95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.95\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and the lowest invocation rate (<math id="A5.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.05\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.05</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.05\%</annotation></semantics></math>) among the evaluated settings, while constraining the executed-harm rate to <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.42\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.42</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.42\%</annotation></semantics></math>—safely satisfying the conformal risk target (<math id="A5.SS1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq 5\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq 5\%</annotation></semantics></math>). Because all observed risks in this distribution are well below <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we employ a zoomed <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>-axis (0–3%) for the executed-harm visualization and plot <math id="A5.SS1.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> as an off-scale reference.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>The Effect of Action-Conditioning in the Guardian Model</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next evaluate the importance of action-conditioning. When disabled, the Guardian model scores the global observation state without conditioning on the specific proposed action <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{a}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{a}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. As discussed in the main text, this reduces the Guardian to a generic state-evaluator, severely impairing its ability to resolve visually ambiguous affordances (e.g., distinguishing a benign tap on “Cancel” from a catastrophic tap on “Confirm Transfer” within the same UI context).</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Appendix E Additional Ablation Details ‣ CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> compares action-conditioning ON versus OFF across fixed thresholds and CRC. As <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> increases, both modes exhibit the expected trend: greater coverage and fewer Diagnostician invocations, coupled with an increasing executed-harm rate. For any fixed <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, the ON variant consistently provides higher coverage than OFF (from <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="85.77\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>85.77</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">85.77\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.02\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89.02</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.02\%</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80.47\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>80.47</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80.47\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="87.91\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>87.91</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">87.91\%</annotation></semantics></math>) and lower invocation rates (from <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="14.23\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>14.23</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">14.23\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10.98\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10.98</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10.98\%</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="19.53\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>19.53</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">19.53\%</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12.09\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>12.09</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12.09\%</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
